claims.text: The glass-forming ability of a Cu-Zr alloy can be enhanced by optimizing alloy composition and cooling rate through molecular dynamics simulations.
Cu60Zr40 is the specific composition proposed to improve glass-forming ability.
Rapid cooling is required for the proposed enhancement.
Composition and cooling rate affect short-range order and cluster formation.
Short-range order and cluster formation inhibit the growth of crystalline nuclei.
Short-range order and cluster formation promote formation of a glassy phase.
Optimizing alloy composition and cooling rate reduces the crystallization tendency by suppressing crystalline-nucleus formation.
The intervention will produce a 20% increase in the critical cooling rate for glass formation relative to the baseline.
The baseline is Cu50Zr50 processed at a conventional cooling rate.
A cooling rate below 100 K/s is sufficient to ensure rapid quenching and prevent crystallization.
The magnitude of the glass-forming-ability increase may depend on the particular composition and cooling rate.

contradictions.description: The mechanism asserts reduced crystallization tendency and easier glass formation, but the predicted improvement is expressed as an increase in the critical cooling rate, without explaining how requiring a higher critical rate follows from that mechanism.

The prediction is a 20% change in critical cooling rate, whereas falsification is based on a less-than-5% change in an undefined glass-forming-ability metric; the rule therefore does not directly test the stated quantitative outcome.
